lessons.title: The Crystal Ball
lessons.content_md:
# Predicting the Future 🔮

One of the most powerful things a Data Scientist can do is **Predictive Analytics**.

It sounds like magic, but it's really just math. 

Imagine you want to predict if it will rain tomorrow. You could just guess. Or, you could look at the weather data for the last 100 days. If the data shows that every time the humidity hits 90% and the temperature drops 10 degrees, it rains the next day, you have found a **pattern**.

Now, if you see the humidity hit 90% today, you can confidently predict rain tomorrow.

## Looking Backward to Look Forward

Data Scientists build Machine Learning models that act like a crystal ball. But instead of magic, the crystal ball is powered by historical data.

- **Netflix** looks at the last 100 movies you watched to predict the 101st movie you will want to click on.
- **Banks** look at millions of historical fraudulent transactions to predict if the credit card swipe happening *right now* is a scam.
- **Hospitals** look at historical patient data to predict which patients are at the highest risk of developing a disease.

<flipcard front="🔮 How does Predictive Analytics work?" back="By feeding historical data into a machine learning algorithm to find patterns, and then applying those patterns to new data to predict what will happen next."></flipcard>

<flipcard front="📈 Is the Crystal Ball always right?" back="No. It operates on probabilities, not certainties. It might say there is an 85% chance of rain, but there is always a margin of error."></flipcard>
